title: receiveTypingIndicators and WSS chatIds filter are parallel suppression mechanisms with no reconciliation
description:
There are two independent ways to suppress typing indicators for a given chat:
1. Chat.receiveTypingIndicators = false (persistent, per-Chat, cross-device, stored server-side)
2. Omitting a chatId from the chatIds list in ChatStreamEnable (per-connection, session-scoped, not persisted)

The spec never explains the relationship between these two mechanisms or when to use which. A client author reading both documents will encounter:
- receiveTypingIndicators: described as an owner-side preference, not shared with peers
- ChatStreamEnable chatIds: described as scoping delivery to a specific view

These serve different purposes semantically (persistent user preference vs. transient view scope), but neither document states this distinction. A server implementer might incorrectly implement one as a fallback for the other. A client implementer might not realize both need to be considered.

The spec should add a note clarifying the intended relationship: receiveTypingIndicators is a persistent, cross-device user preference; chatIds scoping is a session-level UI optimization. Servers enforce both independently. Clients that want to persistently opt out use receiveTypingIndicators; clients that want to scope delivery to an open window use chatIds.

Relevant locations: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md Chat.receiveTypingIndicators field; draft-atwood-jmap-chat-wss-00.md ChatStreamEnable section.
